title: Testing strategy, code coverage, quality gates, and static analysis
objectives: Separate a testing strategy (unit, integration, UAT) from the production deploy coverage gate.
State default production test execution when a deployment contains Apex, and how test levels change that.
Use coverage as a quality gate without treating 75% as a substitute for assertions or UAT.
Place static analysis (Salesforce Code Analyzer) before a metadata deploy, not instead of Apex tests.
diagnostic_question: A production metadata deploy of LAB_ Apex failed coverage. Local tests were green in a sandbox that ran no tests by default. What do you check first: test level, specified-test per-class coverage, missing tests, or static analysis?
definition: A testing strategy decides which Apex tests, UI tests, and human UAT run when. Code coverage is the percentage of Apex executed by tests and is a production deployment gate when Apex is in the payload. Quality gates are the automated fail conditions (tests, coverage, static analysis) that block a metadata deploy. Static analysis inspects source without running it. ([Running Tests in a Deployment](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_meta.meta/api_meta/meta_deploy_running_tests.htm); [project deploy validate](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/salesforce-cli-reference/guide/cli_reference_project_deploy_validate.html); [Salesforce Code Analyzer](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/salesforce-code-analyzer/guide/code-analyzer.html))
why_it_matters: Sandboxes often do not run tests on deploy. Teams that only watch a sandbox green light fail production. Interviewers want RunLocalTests versus RunSpecifiedTests coverage math, and they want to hear that coverage is not quality by itself.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a pre-flight inspection. Unit tests are the walkaround. Coverage is how much of the airframe the walkaround actually touched. Quality gates are 'no takeoff until the board is green.' Static analysis is the hangar X-ray before engines start. UAT is a passenger flight in a sandbox backlot, not the X-ray. A sandbox that skipped tests is a hangar that never rolled the plane outside.
deeper_explanation: When no test level is specified, production runs all local tests (not tests from managed packages) if the deployment package contains Apex classes or triggers. If the package has no Apex, no tests run by default. You can override with a test level. Salesforce recommends running all local tests in a development environment such as a sandbox before production. ([Running Tests in a Deployment](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_meta.meta/api_meta/meta_deploy_running_tests.htm))

CLI test levels include RunLocalTests (validate's default), RunAllTestsInOrg (includes managed-package tests), RunSpecifiedTests, and RunRelevantTests (beta). For RunSpecifiedTests, executed tests must comprise a minimum of 75% coverage for each class and trigger in the deployment package, computed individually—not the same as overall org coverage. ([project deploy validate](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/salesforce-cli-reference/guide/cli_reference_project_deploy_validate.html))

A testing strategy still needs assertions, negative tests, and UAT of metadata behavior (Flows, layouts) that coverage will not see. Coverage is a gate, not a strategy. Tests that insert records create business data in the test context; they do not replace DEVOPS-001 data migration.

Salesforce Code Analyzer is the official static analysis product for Salesforce source (engine details are versioned—reverify the current guide). Run it on Git source before deploy. It does not replace Apex tests or Metadata Coverage. Quality gates in CI should fail the pipeline on analyzer errors you adopted, test failures, and coverage failures—not only on compile.

mental_model.analogy: Pre-flight inspection: tests = walkaround, coverage = how much surface you actually touched, quality gates = no-takeoff board, static analysis = hangar X-ray, UAT = a real flight in a sandbox lot. Skipping sandbox tests is never leaving the hangar.
useful_mapping: Apex unit tests → walkaround of code paths
code coverage → percent of Apex touched
RunSpecifiedTests 75% per class/trigger in the payload → each part's own inspection stamp
RunLocalTests → all local tests except managed-package tests
sandbox default no tests → hangar that did not inspect
where_it_breaks: Airplanes do not have managed-package tests you usually skip.
75% is a documented specified-test rule, not a promise of bug-free Apex.
Flows and layouts need UAT the X-ray will not fly.
Numeric org-wide production coverage requirements can be stated in Help; reverify before quoting a single number as universal.

claims.claim: When no test level is specified on a production deploy, all local tests except managed-package tests run if the payload contains Apex classes or triggers. If it contains no Apex, no tests run by default.

RunSpecifiedTests requires a minimum of 75% coverage for each class and trigger in the deployment package, computed individually. Validate defaults to RunLocalTests and should not be used on sandboxes; use dry-run with RunLocalTests there.
Salesforce Code Analyzer is the official static analysis toolset for Salesforce source and finds issues without executing Apex tests.
Apex is not developed in production. Compile-on-deploy is enabled automatically for production and full sandboxes.

changed_in_release: RunRelevantTests remains beta in the CLI validate reference as of this verification. Code Analyzer major versions change CLIs; reverify.
unresolved_uncertainty: Org-wide 75% production coverage is widely taught; this pack cites the specified-test per-component 75% from the CLI reference and default local-test execution from Metadata API. Confirm any additional Help coverage numbers before quoting them as universal.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Strategy is what you test. Coverage is a production gate when Apex is in the payload. Default production runs local tests if Apex is present. Specified tests need 75% per class and trigger in the package. Static analysis is extra X-ray, not a substitute. Sandboxes may not run tests unless you ask.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I never trust a sandbox deploy that used default no-tests. I dry-run with RunLocalTests or run tests in a scratch org. For production I pick a test level on purpose. If we use specified tests I explain the per-class 75% trap. I add Code Analyzer on the Git source. I still schedule UAT for Flow and layout metadata. Coverage without assertions is not a strategy.

terminology.plain: Which tests run, when, and what they must prove.
terminology.precise: A plan covering Apex unit tests, integration tests, static analysis, and human UAT. Not the same as a single coverage percentage.
terminology.example: Scratch org unit tests on every PR; UAT of LAB_ Flow in a sandbox before production.
terminology.non_example: Shipping because coverage was 76% with empty test methods.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Quality gate: the automated fail line.
terminology.boundary: Jest for LWC is neighboring; this lesson centers Apex deploy tests.

terminology.plain: How much Apex the tests actually executed.
terminology.precise: For RunSpecifiedTests, executed tests must cover at least 75% of each class and trigger in the deployment package, individually.
terminology.example: A new LAB_ trigger at 10% coverage fails specified-test deploy even if org-wide coverage looks high.
terminology.non_example: Covering a Flow by opening it in Setup.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Test pass/fail: a test can pass with low coverage of other classes.
terminology.boundary: See CLI reference for the specified-test rule; do not invent other percentages.

terminology.plain: An automated rule that blocks the metadata deploy.
terminology.precise: Pipeline conditions such as Apex test failure, coverage failure, or static-analysis errors you chose to enforce.
terminology.example: CI fails if Code Analyzer errors or RunLocalTests fail on a scratch org.
terminology.non_example: A CAB meeting with no technical checks.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Approval process on a record (AUTO track).
terminology.boundary: Human approvals for production are DEVOPS-007.

terminology.plain: Reading the source for defects without running it.
terminology.precise: Salesforce Code Analyzer inspects Salesforce source. It does not execute org Apex tests or deploy metadata.
terminology.example: Analyzer flags a hardcoded secret in LAB_ Apex before deploy.
terminology.boundary: Engine set depends on analyzer version.

terminology.plain: Run all tests in the org except those from installed managed and unlocked packages.
terminology.precise: CLI test level; default for project deploy validate.
terminology.example: sf project deploy start --dry-run --test-level RunLocalTests --target-org lab-sandbox
terminology.non_example: RunAllTestsInOrg, which includes managed package tests.
terminology.boundary: Unlocked package tests are excluded per the CLI wording—reverify if your org relies on packaged tests.

terminology.plain: Run only the tests you list.
terminology.precise: Coverage is computed per class and trigger in the deployment package at a 75% minimum each, different from overall percentage.
terminology.example: Deploying one class with one test class named in --tests.
terminology.non_example: Assuming org-wide 80% saves a 0% new trigger in the payload.
terminology.boundary: Must actually list tests that cover the payload.

terminology.plain: Salesforce's official static analysis product for project source.
terminology.precise: Documented analyzer for Salesforce source. Run against Git, not as a replacement for deploy tests.
terminology.example: CI step scanning force-app before project deploy start.
terminology.non_example: Metadata Coverage report, which is type support, not code quality.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Apex PMD as a historical engine name—confirm current analyzer engines.
terminology.boundary: Reverify CLI for the major version installed.

terminology.plain: The org recompiles Apex as part of the metadata deploy.
terminology.precise: Enabled automatically for production and full sandboxes; optional in other org types via Apex Settings.
terminology.example: Deploying a custom field recompiles classes that use it in production.
terminology.non_example: Static analysis compile in CI without an org.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Test execution stage after component deploy.
terminology.boundary: Slight deploy-time cost versus runtime compile surprises.

interview_questions.question: What tests run on a production metadata deploy by default?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: If the payload contains Apex classes or triggers, all local tests except managed-package tests. If there is no Apex, no tests run unless you set a test level.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I cite Running Tests in a Deployment. I mention API 34+ changed object-only packages. I recommend running local tests in sandbox first. I do not quote unofficial numbers for org-wide coverage unless I have Help open. I separate this from validate's required tests.
interview_questions.example: Deploying LAB_GateService.cls to production runs local tests; deploying only a layout does not, by default.
tradeoffs: Time of full local tests versus specified tests
Object-only speed versus hidden Apex later

interview_questions.question: Explain RunSpecifiedTests like an interviewer wants.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Only named tests run, but each class and trigger in the deployment package still needs 75% coverage from those tests, individually—not one org-wide average.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Teams use it to save time and then fail a new trigger at 10%. I insist the test list covers every Apex type in the zip. I contrast RunLocalTests as validate's default. I never use specified tests to hide failing tests in the org.
interview_questions.example: Payload: class + trigger. Tests must cover both to 75%, not just the class.
tradeoffs: Relevant tests beta versus specified lists

interview_questions.question: Sandbox went green, production failed thousands of tests. Why?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The sandbox deploy likely ran no tests. Production saw Apex in the payload and ran local tests. Dry-run with RunLocalTests next time.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I inspect both deploy reports for test counts. I do not blame 'flaky production.' I add a quality gate on PR scratch orgs. I still look at the actual failing tests—some may be real org data assumptions (SeeAllData) that sandbox lacked.
interview_questions.example: Sandbox deploy of LAB_ Apex in 40 seconds with 0 tests; production runs 800 local tests.
tradeoffs: Always RunLocalTests in sandbox versus time
follow_ups: How do you fail CI on zero tests?
weak_answer_warnings: Production is broken because it runs tests

interview_questions.question: Coverage is 82% and the VP wants to skip UAT. Your answer?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Coverage is an Apex gate, not a strategy. Flows, layouts, and permissions need UAT. Empty tests can inflate coverage.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I show a Flow that coverage never executed. I offer a short UAT script in a sandbox. I add Code Analyzer so we are not only measuring lines. I do not insult coverage; I put it in its box.
interview_questions.example: LAB_ boarding Flow inactive after deploy; coverage never opened the Flow.
tradeoffs: Automated UI tests versus human UAT
follow_ups: How do you test Flow in CI?

interview_questions.question: Where does Salesforce Code Analyzer sit in the quality gates?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: On the Git source, before or beside org tests. It is static analysis. It does not replace Apex tests or Metadata Coverage.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I run it on PRs so secrets and simple defects fail fast without spinning an org. I pin the analyzer major version because engines change. Failures need a policy: fix, or suppress with reason, not delete the step. I still deploy to a scratch org and run tests.
interview_questions.example: PR check: analyzer on force-app, then scratch deploy plus RunLocalTests.

interview_questions.question: What is a quality gate in Salesforce DevOps?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: An automated fail-closed check—tests, coverage, analyzer—that blocks metadata deploy. It is not a Flow approval or a CAB meeting.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I list the gates for this team: analyzer, unit tests, coverage rule matching the test level, maybe lint for LWC. Human approvals belong to pipelines. I keep data-migration checks on the data pipeline, not as Apex coverage.
interview_questions.example: Jenkins fails if dry-run RunLocalTests fails, even if Git merged.

interview_questions.question: Specified-test deploy fails coverage. Walk the diagnosis.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: List Apex classes and triggers in the payload. Check each for 75% from the named tests. Add tests or widen the test list. Do not switch to ignore-errors.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I download the coverage report. A helper at 100% does not save a trigger at 0%. I run the same tests in a scratch org first. I consider RunLocalTests if the specified list is a false economy. I still will not ship empty tests.
interview_questions.example: LAB_GateTrigger 12% covered; add a test method that inserts LAB_Gate__c rows in test context.
tradeoffs: More tests vs broader test level
follow_ups: How do you see coverage in CLI?
weak_answer_warnings: Ignore coverage for hotfixes as a habit

interview_questions.question: Design a testing strategy for a release that is 70% Flow and 30% Apex.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Apex: unit tests plus an explicit deploy test level. Flow: sandbox UAT and activation checks. Analyzer on source. Do not let Apex coverage stand in for the Flow.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I split metadata types. I run local tests because Apex is in the payload. I add a Flow test interview or human script. I watch that a Flow-only follow-up deploy would run no tests by default—so I may still set a test level if Apex in the org could break. I keep data fixtures synthetic.
interview_questions.example: PR: analyzer + scratch Apex tests. UAT sandbox: run LAB_ boarding Flow as the target user.
tradeoffs: Always running local tests vs payload-based defaults
follow_ups: Permission set for the UAT user?
